justification: citation_proof.py decides whether a DCP section number is shown to users (frontend-nextjs/lib/citation-display.ts). Re-judging 368 numbers found wrong on the live PDFs on 2026-10-30 showed 57 of them had been shown as proven/imprecise. Six leaks closed; shown-wrong falls to 3 (two print identical words under two sections, one is a doubtful renumber the checker now withholds).

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Restoring origin/main scripts/citation_proof.py fails 10 tests (8 new, 1 unmarked former strict-xfail, 1 page-proven test); measured. Bench on live R2 PDFs (~/.claude/plans/ce-devtype-evidence-2026-10-29/bench/bench.py): known_wrong shown 57 -> 3, known_right proven 1017 -> 1016.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The council PDFs in R2 (cached lines v5 incl. bookmarks); known-wrong set = numbers corrected today after page-text + Sonnet checks with quoted headings.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: git show origin/main:scripts/citation_proof.py over the file, then pytest tests/test_citation_proof.py: 10 failed / 42 passed. Restored: 55 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured on 368 known-wrong and 1,688 known-right rows against live R2 PDFs (bench_baseline: 57 wrong numbers shown).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Old proof accepted a code named in ANY page's running header, and could not see heading numbers printed as pictures.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends citation_proof.py in place; no new module, no schema change.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A PDF that cannot be read stays verdict no_source in dcp_citation_status (unchanged); a PDF with no bookmarks gets an empty outline and the new checks are skipped, not failed.
pre_impl.frontend_type: citation_status is a text column read by frontend-nextjs/lib/citation-display.ts; only proven and imprecise are shown, so the change can only hide numbers, never invent one.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A wrong verdict of not_proven hides a correct section number and the user sees the page reference only; a wrong proven shows a wrong clause number, which this change reduces from 57 to 3 on the bench.

functions.name: restore_outline_numbers
functions.input: the PDF's own text lines with page and position, plus its bookmark list of level, title and page
functions.output: lines with the bookmark's number prefixed where only its title is printed
functions.if_none: no bookmarks or broken ones -> lines unchanged

functions.name: outline_allows
functions.input: the chapter's built lines with its bookmark page ranges, a section code, and one page number
functions.output: True/False/None whether bookmarks place the page in that section
functions.if_none: when the PDF has no usable bookmarks it returns None and every caller skips the bookmark check entirely

functions.name: prove_citation
functions.input: a stored reference number, the stored rule text, one reading of the chapter lines, a page hint and whether that page is proven
functions.output: a status of proven, imprecise, not_proven, unjudged or text_not_found with a short detail naming the failing heading
functions.if_none: when the rule's wording cannot be found anywhere in the PDF it returns text_not_found and the number is not shown

values.if_missing: no evidence the stricter checker removes wrong numbers

queries.sql: SELECT id, pdf_page FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE id = ANY(%s) AND page_check IN ('on_page','moved')
queries.purpose: Find which served rules have a stored page proven to hold them, so the proof judges repeated wording on that page only.
queries.where_clause: id = ANY(served ids) AND page_check IN ('on_page','moved') -- read-only, no write

break_it.scenario: City of Sydney bookmarks all point to page 1
break_it.what_happens: every section would be placed on page 1 and good numbers rejected
break_it.how: outline_entries returns [] when all numbered entries share a page

break_it.scenario: A bookmark title also appears inside a sentence on its page
break_it.what_happens: a number would be glued onto prose and become a fake heading
break_it.how: only a line equal to the title, exactly once on that page

break_it.scenario: Unchecked stored page points at the wrong copy of repeated wording
break_it.what_happens: a correct section number would be rejected because the wrong copy was judged
break_it.how: the page narrows the search only when page_check proved it

break_it.scenario: Running header names the chapter on every page and the number is chapter plus an unchecked item
break_it.what_happens: C1.3 passed for Woollahra rules that are printed under C1.2.3 instead
break_it.how: header evidence only for a plain section reading and only on the rule's page

break_it.scenario: City of Sydney rule text opens with the parent site's preamble before its sub-heading
break_it.what_happens: the run-on rule could reject the correct sub-heading
break_it.how: a heading inside the span is accepted when the rule opened under its parent

break_it.scenario: The query that finds served rules with a proven stored page returns a stale page_check (rule moved since)
break_it.what_happens: the proof would judge only the copy on an outdated page and could reject a correct number
break_it.how: if no copy of the wording lies on that page the narrowing falls back to every copy (here or anchors)

mutation_analysis: Old code: 10 tests fail; new: 55 pass.
residual_risk: Test sets come from today's own methods; bookmarks trusted when not obviously broken; 1 known-right row (122395) now page-only. Cache key bumped to v5, so the next status run re-reads every PDF (slow, OCR).
